Painkiller components vary but generally fall into acetaminophen, Nonsteroidal Anti-Inflammatory Drugs (NSAIDs) like ibuprofen/naproxen, or weaker opioids (codeine, oxycodone) for stronger relief, often combined with caffeine for enhanced effect. 

The core active ingredients target pain and inflammation, while inactive components ensure proper delivery (tablets, gels). 

Common Active Ingredients (Analgesics)

Acetaminophen: (Tylenol) Reduces pain and fever, found in many OTC/prescription meds.

NSAIDs (Nonsteroidal Anti-Inflammatory Drugs): Reduce pain, fever, and inflammation.
Ibuprofen: (Advil, Motrin).
Naproxen Sodium: (Aleve).
Aspirin: (Acetylsalicylic Acid).

Opioids: Stronger prescription pain relievers that alter pain perception in the brain.

Codeine, Oxycodone, Morphine: Often combined with other drugs. 
Combination Ingredients

Caffeine: Added to some pain relievers (like Excedrin) to boost the effects of acetaminophen or aspirin, notes this WebMD article. 

Other Components (Inactive/Excipients)
Binders, Fillers, Coatings: These inactive ingredients help form the tablet, control how it dissolves, and give it color or taste, as seen in this description of a pain relief product. 

Types of Formulations

Single-Ingredient: Contains just acetaminophen or one NSAID.

Compound/Combination: Mixes ingredients like acetaminophen and codeine (Co-codamol) or acetaminophen, aspirin, and caffeine (Excedrin).
